Name: uav_night_self_training
Title: Unlabeled real night images or realistic synthetic darkness: what improves small-object detection in night UAV imagery?
Short Hypothesis: With the share of replaced training images held fixed at 12.6% (496 of 3945), (H1, primary) self-training YOLO11s on unlabeled real night UAV images pseudo-labelled by its own day-trained model (arm D) raises COCO AP for objects under 32x32 px on held-out real night clips over day-only training (arm A), closing part of the gap to training on labelled night images (arm C); (H2) a spatially varying synthetic night model with light pools, a sodium colour cast and sensor noise (B_full) raises it over A and over the global darkening of the earlier study (B_global).
Related Work: VisDrone2019-DET (Zhu et al., 'Detection and Tracking Meet Drones Challenge', TPAMI 2022) is a dense aerial benchmark dominated by small objects and has no illumination labels, so night subsets are built ad hoc; Liu et al. (Frontiers in AI 2025, PFNN) compare enhancers on a VisDrone night subset without size-stratified metrics. Physics-inspired synthesis that unprocesses, darkens, adds shot/read noise and re-applies the ISP (MAET, Cui et al., ICCV 2021; evaluated after fine-tuning on ExDark) and noise-based low-light simulation (Lv et al., IJCV 2021) provide synthetic dark training data; DAI-Net (Du et al., CVPR 2024) trains only on well-lit data with paired MAET-style dark copies and reports that training a face detector directly on the synthetic images lowered precision on DARK FACE (15.2 to 11.6). Enhancers such as Zero-DCE (Guo et al., CVPR 2020) and Zero-DCE++ (Li et al., TPAMI 2021) need no paired data; IA-YOLO (Liu et al., AAAI 2022), FeatEnHancer (Hashmi et al., ICCV 2023) and YOLA (Hong et al., NeurIPS 2024) couple illumination handling to the detector. The UG2+ benchmark (Yang et al., TIP 2020) found enhancement does not always help detection, and YOLA reports that several enhancers lower YOLOv3 mAP50 on ExDark (Loh & Chan, CVIU 2019) and can impair details of tiny faces. Related aerial and night work includes RGB-infrared vehicle detection on DroneVehicle (Sun et al., TCSVT 2022), nighttime aerial tracking adaptation (UDAT, Ye et al., CVPR 2022), day-to-night detector adaptation that targets small low-light objects (2PCNet, Kennerley et al., CVPR 2023) and slicing-based small-object inference (SAHI, Akyon et al., ICIP 2022). Self-training with pseudo-labels from a source-trained teacher is a standard unsupervised domain adaptation baseline for detection (e.g., mean-teacher and pseudo-label methods such as 2PCNet, which targets day-to-night adaptation); here it is used in its simplest single-round form. An earlier study in this project (v1, 2026-09-30) found that calibrated global synthetic darkness did not improve real night small-object AP (B - A = -0.0053 over three seeds, clip-bootstrap intervals including zero), while 496 labelled night images did (+0.0133); at a matched 12.5% replacement share the night deficit remained. To our knowledge no study compares unlabeled real night images with realistic synthetic night for UAV small objects at a matched replacement share on a clip-disjoint split; this is not a verified novelty claim.
Abstract: USE THE SUPPORT FILES: uavlib.py (version 2.0) and uav_splits.json are next to the script; import uavlib and follow the Code To Use example. uavlib fixes the protocol and must not be re-implemented or modified: the pre-registered clip-level image groups (identical to the earlier study: day_train 3945, day_tune 482, day_test 1443, night_train 496, night_test 744 in 24 clips, twilight_test 393; prepare() verifies these counts), annotation handling (VisDrone ignored regions and 'others' are crowd regions for every class), the synthetic low-light model, pseudo-labelling, test-time enhancement, COCO evaluation and bootstraps. Never read night_test or twilight_test for training, tuning, early stopping or model selection; print their metrics prefixed report_only. DATA: uavlib.prepare() downloads the Ultralytics VisDrone zips once per VM into /content/cache/visdrone and caches every step; do not copy datasets or weights into ./working. ARMS (uavlib.build_training_set; identical model, schedule, augmentation, seed and 3945 training images; B, C and D each replace exactly 496 day_train images, 12.6%, uavlib.matched_fraction): A = day_train unchanged; B_global = 496 seeded day images replaced by calibrated global synthetic low-light copies (arm='B'; the earlier study's generator); B_full = the same 496 day images replaced by synthetic copies with spatially varying light pools, a sodium colour cast and Poisson-Gaussian noise (arm='B', pools=True, cast=True); C = 496 day images replaced by all night_train images with their labels (a labelled-night reference, not a method); D = the same day images as C replaced by the same night_train images labelled ONLY with pseudo-labels from this seed's arm-A model (uavlib.pseudo_label(weights_A, data, imgsz) at the pre-registered confidence uavlib.PSEUDO_CONF = 0.25; build_training_set(data, 'D', seed, pseudo=pseudo)). D never uses night_train ground truth; pseudo_label's diagnostic_vs_ground_truth is report-only and must not choose anything. Train A first, then D from A's weights. DETECTOR AND SCHEDULE (fixed, not tuned): Ultralytics YOLO11s from COCO-pretrained yolo11s.pt via uavlib.train, 16 epochs, imgsz 1280, batch 16 (the earlier study's tuned schedule), device 0, val=False, final weights evaluated; never call .to(device) on a YOLO object. uavlib.train reuses a model trained earlier on the same VM with identical inputs (training is deterministic at a fixed seed); its info has cached=True then, which is expected. EVALUATION: uavlib.evaluate at imgsz 1280 on day_tune, synth_dark_tune, day_test, synth_dark_test, night_test and twilight_test; night_test is also evaluated with test-time gamma and CLAHE (uavlib does this). Metrics are COCO AP (IoU 0.50:0.95) and AP50 at original resolution, maxDets 500, per area bin: tiny < 16^2, small 16^2-32^2, small_all < 32^2 (PRIMARY), medium 32^2-96^2, large. For every arm save the night_test state with uavlib.save_state(result['night_test']['none']['state'], 'working/state_<arm>_night_test.npy') so later stages and offline analyses can compare models; these files are expected outputs. Report-only comparisons on night_test small_all AP: paired clip bootstrap (uavlib.paired_clip_bootstrap, 1000 resamples of the 24 night_test clips) for D-A (H1), B_full-A and B_full-B_global (H2), B_global-A, C-A (reference) and D-C; leave-one-clip-out (uavlib.leave_one_clip_out) for D-A, B_full-A and C-A; gap closure (D-A)/(C-A) and (B_full-A)/(C-A), interpreted only when C-A clearly exceeds zero. Day guard: report each arm's day_test small_all AP change versus A (a loss of more than 0.01 is a guard failure, which is a study outcome, not a bug). Also report the change from test-time gamma and CLAHE on night_test small_all and medium AP per arm, and pseudo-label counts. SELECTION: no hyperparameter or arm is selected in this study. selection_AP_small_all = arm A's small_all AP on day_tune is an implementation check only (higher means a correct, complete run); it never ranks arms. SEEDS: read the training seed from os.environ.get('AUTORESEARCH_SEED', '0') (default 0 is required: the evaluated stage-3 script is reused as seed 0 and the harness reruns seeds 1 and 2); splits and synthetic evaluation sets stay fixed. COMPUTE: the whole study has a hard cap of 75 Colab compute units; an A100 costs about 5.4 units per hour and an L4 about 1.7. Declare L4 for the stage-1 pilot and A100 for full-schedule scripts. Measured in the earlier study on an A100 at 1280 px: about 44 s per epoch (about 12 minutes per 16-epoch arm) and about 6 minutes to evaluate one model on all groups with enhancements; data preparation under 2 minutes once per VM. A five-arm full script therefore takes about 90 minutes. Only the 150-minute hard limit is binding: a script that completes within it with correct, finite results is NOT buggy, and runtime alone must never be reported as a bug. Results that fail a hypothesis or the guard are study outcomes, not bugs. OUTPUT: save working/experiment_data.npy with settings, environment (uavlib.environment()), counts, clips, per-arm train info, arm info and metrics (uavlib.strip_states), pseudo-label stats, the bootstrap and leave-one-clip-out results and runtime; print a compact summary. Plotting and metric parsing run locally with only numpy and matplotlib. Never fabricate or estimate a metric that was not computed. Short fine-tuning schedules make absolute AP incomparable with published VisDrone results; only within-study comparisons are claimed.
Experiments: Stage 1 (pilot, L4, about 45 min): run the Code To Use example (arms A, B_global, B_full, C, D at 3 epochs and 640 px) and verify the printed group counts, finite metrics for every group, 496 replaced images in B_global, B_full, C and D, the saved night_test state files, pseudo-label counts and seconds per epoch.

Stage 2 (A100, about 25 min, no tuning): run arm A only at the fixed full schedule (16 epochs, 1280 px, seed 0), pseudo-label night_train with it and report the pseudo-label counts, seconds per epoch and evaluation time, and project the five-arm stage-3 runtime. Do not change the schedule, model, data, arms or evaluation.

Stage 3 (main comparison, A100, about 90 min): all five arms at the fixed full schedule for one seed per script (the harness reuses the evaluated script as seed 0 and reruns seeds 1 and 2); evaluate all groups; save the night_test states; report every pre-registered comparison, leave-one-clip-out, gap closures, the day guard, test-time enhancement changes and pseudo-label stats. Extra analyses of the same runs are allowed (per-class AP, twilight_test).

Stage 4 (ablations, seed 0, full schedule, two variants per script, about 40-60 min, evaluated exactly as in stage 3; compare with the stage-3 seed-0 results that the harness copies into ./parent_results/ (experiment_data.npy and state_<arm>_night_test.npy files), and do not retrain arms B_global, C or D): in this order, (1) the B_full components: light pools without the cast (arm='B', pools=True) and the cast without pools (arm='B', cast=True); (2) the pseudo-label threshold of D at conf 0.10 and 0.50 (teacher: the seed-0 arm-A model; retrain arm A at seed 0 if the VM cache does not hold it); (3) B_full at replacement fractions 0.25 and 0.5.
Report negative and null results; state effect sizes with seed ranges and clip-bootstrap intervals rather than claiming significance.
Risk Factors and Limitations: night_test is the same set used in the earlier study, and these hypotheses were written after its results were seen; B_full was pre-registered there as an ablation but never ran, and D is new.
Night is defined by a per-image luminance threshold plus a visual clip audit, not capture metadata; 8 mostly-daylight clips had dark frames reclassified as twilight.
night_test has 24 clips, but five clips hold 677 of its 744 images, so clip-level variation dominates and bootstrap intervals are wide; night_train has only 15 clips.
Pseudo-labels from a day-trained teacher miss many small night objects; missed objects are trained as background, which can hurt recall.
Arms C and D add 15 night clips of new scene content, so their gains mix illumination with content; location overlap between night_train and night_test clips was not checked.
The synthetic night model is hand-designed (light pools, a single sodium cast, uncalibrated noise); it is not a learned or camera-calibrated simulator.

Fine-tuning schedules are short relative to published work, so absolute AP is not comparable; three training seeds do not capture dataset variability; conclusions are limited to VisDrone and one detector.
Stage-4 ablations use one seed; clip-bootstrap intervals cover test-clip sampling only.

Stage Goals.1:
- Get the five-arm pilot in the experiment plan working with uavlib exactly as in Code To Use
- Verify group counts, 496 replaced images in B_global, B_full, C and D, finite metrics, saved night_test state files and timings
- Use only VisDrone through uavlib; do not add datasets
Stage Goals.2:
- Run arm A only at the fixed full schedule (16 epochs, 1280 px, seed 0) and pseudo-label night_train with it
- DO NOT tune or change the schedule, model, data, arms or evaluation; do not add datasets
- Report seconds per epoch, evaluation time and pseudo-label counts so the five-arm stage-3 script fits 150 minutes
Stage Goals.3:
- Run the pre-registered main comparison (arms A, B_global, B_full, C, D) at the fixed full schedule, with saved night_test states, paired clip bootstraps and leave-one-clip-out
- Improvements may only fix bugs, improve efficiency or add analyses of the same runs; do not change arms, splits, metrics or the schedule; do not add datasets
Stage Goals.4:
- Train only the pre-specified variants in the experiment plan, two per script, at the full schedule and seed 0
- Compare with the stage-3 seed-0 results in ./parent_results/ instead of retraining the main arms; evaluate exactly as in stage 3; do not add datasets
